finding: US patients reported more neurocognitive, GI and PEM impairment than Japanese patients on DSQ; Japanese women had worse SF-36 function than Japanese men.
NK cytotoxicity assay comparison (Cr51, flow, CD107a) on shipped vs same-day blood to identify assay formats tolerant of shipping.
GETSET guided graded exercise self-help: short-term fatigue gain maintained at 15 months but no longer differed from specialist care; no main effect after multiplicity adjustment.
note: Mixed CFS criteria; open-label, self-report outcomes

finding: Adolescents with CFS/ME still disabled after 12 months described barriers of poor awareness, stigma and need for holistic support.
Tarlov (perineural) cysts on MRI in 39% of FM/CFS patients (42% women, 12% men), about three times general population rate.
note: Retrospective, mixed FM/CFS (CDC 1994), no control group

finding: Protocol for an overview of systematic reviews of acupuncture for CFS.
Systematic review of IV vitamin C for fatigue: 3 of 4 controlled trials and 4 of 5 uncontrolled studies showed fatigue reduction; not long COVID trials.

Fecal microbiota of CFS/ME showed reduced Lachnospiraceae (Anaerostipes) and more Bacteroides and Phascolarctobacterium; fecal metabolomics showed higher glutamic and argininosuccinic acid and lower alpha-tocopherol.
note: Small Italian cohort; sample size not in abstract

finding: Six-week supervised adapted pulmonary rehabilitation improved shuttle walk distance (+112 m), fatigue and cognition with no worsening events.
note: No controls, no PEM selection; preprint

finding: Re-analysis found hypomethylated ACE/ACE2 probes in ME/CFS but no difference in ACE or ACE2 gene expression in meta-analysis or in PBMCs.
Perspective on Ross River virus immune evasion and possible links to post-viral fatigue and ME.
Parallel patient surveys on economic impact, care and quality of life in three countries; similar demographics and burden.
Case report of post-COVID POTS with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies and MCAS improving with directed therapy.
Different ME/CFS case definitions agree poorly; simulation shows misclassification affects association analyses.
Fatigue/fibromyalgia-like symptom scores in end-stage renal disease correlated with urea, copper, Wnt pathway proteins.
Heart-rate-variability based NOL index showed dissociation over time in post-COVID fatigue participants vs controls (p=0.046), suggesting dysautonomia.
Activity diary correlated only weakly with accelerometer-measured activity (rs about 0.35-0.38) in female CFS patients.
Parent survey of children with long COVID: 54% reported PEM, 80% fatigue, only 10% back to previous activity; 8.2 months mean duration.
Statistical mixture-model method for herpesvirus serology illustrated with ME/CFS data.
Intracerebroventricular TGF-beta1 in mice induced fatigue-like behaviour, raised LDH/CK and reduced tyrosine hydroxylase and striatal dopamine.
note: Mouse model; relevance to patient TGF-beta unclear

finding: Protocol for systematic review of circulating leptin in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia.
Systematic review: CBT was the most evaluated intervention and judged cost-effective in three trials for adults; other evidence limited.
note: Economic evaluations derived from RCTs with known outcome-measure limits

finding: Maximal exercise did not produce the post-exercise reduction in augmentation index seen in controls at 48 h, suggesting absent exercise-induced vasodilation in ME/CFS; no baseline arterial stiffness difference.
note: Small, split into 48 h and 72 h groups

finding: EUROMENE experts perceived widespread GP lack of knowledge, with about 60% of patients undiagnosed.
Opinion proposing ME/CFS and long-haul COVID be grouped as post active phase of infection syndromes (PAPIS) with shared oxidative and mitochondrial pathology.
Recursive ensemble feature selection found a 23-gene PBMC signature (AUC 0.92, 0.95 on another platform) and 48 CpGs (AUC 0.97) separating cases from controls.
note: Re-analysis of public data, risk of overfitting, small control group

finding: Hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 raises methyl-group demand, resembling B12 deficiency, possibly explaining long COVID and ME/CFS symptoms.
Systematic review: six of nine nutraceutical studies targeting mitochondria reported fatigue improvement; quality limited.
MERS survivors with chronic fatigue at 12 months had higher suicidality risk over 2 years (RR 7.5, 95% CI 2.4-23.1).
Parent and child reports of anxiety and depression on RCADS showed reasonable agreement in paediatric CFS/ME.
Plasma FGF21 and NT-proBNP higher in ME/CFS, with lower antioxidant capacity, higher lipoperoxides and raised IL-1b, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-a and CRP.
Six months after mild COVID, 41 of 42 had PEM and 19 of 42 met Canadian Consensus Criteria for ME/CFS; those had more fatigue and stress intolerance.
note: Charité Fatigue Center referral sample, no controls

finding: Interviews with five severely affected people described lived experience, daily-life challenges and condition management.
RNA-seq of whole blood and sorted PBMCs gave cell-type-specific CFS signatures overlapping other fatiguing illnesses and network master regulators.
note: Preprint; sample size not in abstract

finding: At 6 months, 2.5% screened positive for CFS (Fukuda questionnaire) and 17.5% had fatigue; PTSD not associated with CFS.
CFS/ME and fibromyalgia groups responded similarly on symptom questionnaires; invariance held except for a few scales.
Protocol for meta-analysis of acupoint catgut embedding for CFS.

Cluster analysis of NorCAPITAL biological markers gave six overlapping clusters (e.g. orthostatic intolerance, low-grade inflammation, high vagal activity); poor-cognition/pain-intolerant cluster had lower function.
Aptamer proteomics (4790 proteins) found 19 differing proteins, highlighting ephrin pathway and immune signalling; AUC above 0.85, up to 0.95 using ratios.
Surface EMG showed muscle fibre conduction velocity increased excessively with force in CFS compared with FM and controls (P=0.01).
Serum exosome-associated mtDNA rose after exercise in ME/CFS and patient exosomes stimulated IL-1b release from cultured human microglia.
note: Preprint, small, n not in abstract

finding: Head-up tilt triggered prolonged increases in pain, fatigue and concentration scores lasting 7 days in ME/CFS, none in controls.
note: Orthostatic stress as PEM trigger; Fukuda/CCC patients

finding: Plasma autoantibodies to CNS proteins distinguished Gulf War illness; sex differences in 8 of 10 markers; ME/CFS used only as symptomatic comparator.
After cognitive exertion, ME/CFS women had increased fatigue and pain and larger insular functional connectivity increases that correlated with symptom worsening.
Very severe (homebound-bedridden) participants differed from homebound ones in the PEM symptom domain.
CSF metabolomics: glutamate higher after exercise in Gulf War illness without postural tachycardia; ME/CFS and GWI differed in lysoPC a C28:0 at rest; no post-exercise ME/CFS samples.
Postal survey: ME/CFS lowered patient quality of life (physical domain worst) and family quality of life, with correlation between the two.

Review of physiotherapy RCTs: effects of exercise-type interventions diminished with narrower case definitions requiring PEM, more objective outcomes and longer follow-up; only one RCT used PEM-required criteria.
Teachers of children aged 5-11 with CFS/ME described varied symptoms and barriers to school support.
Six-week supervised rehabilitation improved shuttle walk distance, fatigue and cognition with no serious adverse events.
Multicomponent exercise in post-acute care improved SPPB and function in post-COVID patients including post-ICU.
note: Post-ICU deconditioning population, not long COVID with PEM

finding: Seven-week virtual interdisciplinary 'Recovering from COVID' course improved health-related quality of life in post-COVID syndrome.
Thesis: meta-analysis found pooled peak VO2 lower in ME/CFS than healthy controls (pooled difference about 5.2 ml/kg/min); also examines physical activity and exercise interventions.
note: Thesis abstract truncated; effect size read from partial text

finding: 81% of FM/ME-CFS patients met Brighton hypermobility criteria (OR 7.08) and 18% met 2017 hEDS criteria.
Nexfin CO Trek finger plethysmography overestimates stroke volume vs suprasternal Doppler during tilt; calibration to Doppler makes it usable.
Russian review of asthenic disorders as CFS with a suggestion that the peptide drug cortexin could be used.
Adaptation and validation of a health anxiety inventory for medical settings, tested in MS, ME/CFS and chronic pain.
Russian review of possible post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome causes and treatment.
Accounts from Royal Free staff of the 1955 outbreak were typical of an infectious illness, arguing against epidemic hysteria.
Literature review: a third to a half of GPs did not accept ME/CFS as a genuine entity and many lacked diagnostic confidence.
Perspective proposing a model of central, psychological and peripheral contributors to post-COVID fatigue.
Post-COVID patients had high fatigue and anhedonia scores that correlated with each other and with time since recovery.
Scoping review of causal-factor research: immunological (297), psychological (243), infection (198), neuroendocrine (198); most studies case-control, over half n<=100.
Gut fungal dysbiosis in tumour-induced cachexia in mice; ME only mentioned as a comparator.
Narrative review of long-haul COVID pathophysiology, risk factors (female sex, early dyspnea, D-dimer) and treatments.
Focus groups in Ireland described healthcare barriers, socioeconomic and disability-related costs.

n: 37 studies, 1016 patients vs 686 controls (ME/CFS and FM)
finding: Perceived exertion during aerobic exercise higher in ME/CFS and FM than controls (Hedges d 0.85, 95% CI 0.62-1.08).
Scoping review of European non-pharmacological therapies: CBT reduced fatigue more than usual care; rehabilitation and pacing results inconsistent.
Maladaptive perfectionism was consistently associated with depression in CFS/ME (r 0.42-0.48).
Daily physical therapy to cervical muscles in hospital reported 55.5% recovery of ME/CFS by self-rating; pupil diameter used for autonomic function.
note: Uncontrolled, self-rated, single Japanese centre, preprint

finding: CSF miRNAs miR-608, -328, -200a-5p, -93-3p, -92a-3p were lower after submaximal exercise, implying altered phosphoinositol signalling and adhesion pathways.
note: Different groups for rest and exercise; informatics inference

finding: Biobanked frozen PBMCs showed no Treg or NK subset differences between ME/CFS and controls, and cryopreservation altered NK markers (CD25, CD69, NKp46).
note: Small; methodological caution for biobank immune markers

finding: Ecological momentary assessment showed heterogeneous fatigue perpetuators across individuals; none predicted CBT outcome.
Rapid resting respiratory rate was predicted by PEM, not psychological or sedentary measures.
Eleven circulating microRNAs differed in severely ill ME/CFS before and after a PEM-inducing stress challenge and related to symptom severity.
Wearable IMU 'UpTime' separated severity: severe under 20% of day upright, moderate 20-30%, controls over 30%.
In fibromyalgia manual physiotherapy, patients with comorbid ME/CFS responded less than FM-only patients; baseline pain threshold predicted response.

Post-hoc analysis of Phase III rintatolimod trial: patients with 2-8 years' illness had over twice the placebo-adjusted treadmill gain; 51.2% improved exercise duration by 25% or more (p=0.003); no response in >8 years.
Review of primary outcomes in CFS/ME RCTs: 96% used patient-reported measures (SF-36, CIS, Chalder most common).
Fukuda CFS patients with higher sympathetic vascular drive, slower reaction time and lower HRmax were less likely to complete a 16-week structured exercise programme; 35 discontinued.
Interviews on paediatric CFS/ME aged 5-11 described complex disability and differing parental roles by child age.
Echocardiographic cardiac dimensions and function (including strain) did not differ between ME/CFS and controls at rest.
In a stress-induced CFS mouse model, pregnancy showed abnormal placenta, oxidative stress and inhibited Wnt/beta-catenin signalling.
note: Mouse stress model of CFS; validity uncertain

finding: NLP framework to extract and classify medication data from ME/CFS study free text.
Plasma EVs 30-130 nm were more abundant in ME/CFS; EV and plasma cytokine profiles examined by 45-plex assay.
Sitting for an hour reduced cerebral blood flow in severe ME/CFS (474 vs 627 mL/min in controls); 90 patients with orthostatic intolerance had -26.9% CBF reduction; supine CBF normal.
note: Extends tilt-based CBF finding to bed-bound patients using milder sitting stress

finding: Serum BDNF higher and BDNF exon 9 methylation lower in CFS with fibromyalgia, with methylation predicting BDNF and symptoms.
note: Comorbid FM; small; methylation findings historically poorly replicated

finding: Cognitive exertion lowered DMN connectivity and raised fatigue similarly in CFS/ME and controls; patients had higher baseline fatigue and poorer cognition.
Laser-evoked potentials in CFS did not differ from controls, arguing against generalised nociceptive CNS hyperexcitability.
EUROMENE recommendations for standardising epidemiological data collection in ME/CFS.
Philosophical commentary on the illness-disease distinction using CFS as example.
PBMC SWATH-MS proteomics: 9 of 11 patients separated from controls by PCA; 60 differentially expressed proteins pointing to deficient ATP production and oxidative stress.
note: Very small; subgroup selected post hoc

finding: Fibromyalgia/CFS-like symptoms in schizophrenia correlate with IL-6, HMGB1 and opioid markers.
35% of adolescents with CFS/ME met criteria for a mental health disorder (20% depression, 27% anxiety); questionnaires moderately accurate.
Patients described variable PEM symptoms in daily life and after CPET, with core themes of exhaustion, cognitive difficulty and neuromuscular complaints.
Meta-ethnography of qualitative literature on support needs, framing invisibility, loss of self and fraught clinical encounters.
Naturalistic CBT clinic: fatigue and function improved (d 0.45-0.91) and 85% self-reported improvement.
note: Uncontrolled, self-report, includes chronic fatigue without ME/CFS

finding: Preprint version of FM manual physiotherapy study: patients with comorbid ME/CFS responded less than FM-only patients.
Head-up tilt lowered pressure pain thresholds in ME/CFS with or without FM but not in controls; windup higher than controls, unchanged by tilt.
note: Orthostatic stress as a hyperalgesia trigger, like exercise

n: 171 GWI vs 60 vs 50 ME/CFS vs 35 IBS
finding: CNS autoantibodies were elevated in Gulf War illness compared with healthy veterans, ME/CFS and IBS; ME/CFS used as symptomatic comparator.
Cistanche plus ginkgo botanical for 60 days reduced Chalder fatigue, memory and PEM symptom scores and lowered blood ammonia and lactate versus placebo.
note: Chinese CFS criteria likely not PEM-defined; preprint; self-report

finding: Philosophical paper on epistemic injustice in healthcare using ME/CFS as a case.
Two-day CPET repeatability in Gulf War illness: ICC at peak 0.84, smallest real difference about 19%, and no group-by-time interaction.
note: Gulf War illness, not ME/CFS; small

finding: Acupuncture plus ginsenoside Rg1 improved swimming endurance and T cell subsets in a rat chronic-stress fatigue model.
Systematic review of structural and functional MRI: inconsistent anatomical differences, more or broader activation on tasks; insufficient data for a neural biomarker.

n: 34 childhood cancer survivors, 102 CFS, 95 adult cancer survivors
finding: Cognitive-behavioural fatigue-maintaining factors overlapped substantially between childhood cancer survivors and CFS patients.
Multivariate plasma and muscle cytokine profiles predicted diagnosis, maximal voluntary contraction, fatigue and cognitive reaction times, with little muscle mitochondrial dysfunction.
Australian cost-of-illness: estimated annual health-care and income-loss cost of AUD 14.5 billion; about 12 GP visits per participant per year.
Actigraphy showed lower daytime activity, higher night-time activity and delayed daytime start in children with ME/CFS; self-report correlated with ActiGraph.
ICC clinical severity grades tracked SF-36 physical function (70/43/15), steps/day (8235/5195/2031) and CPET ventilatory-threshold VO2 across mild/moderate/severe.
Internal pilot of a trial of internet-delivered CBT (FITNET-NHS) for adolescents with CFS/ME assessing recruitment feasibility.
Framework for ME/CFS natural history from predisposition through prodrome to a late hypometabolic state, with a hypermetabolic early neuro-immune phase.
Exercise changed N-back fMRI activation in ME/CFS (increased midbrain, operculo-insular and insula) but not controls; GWI showed deactivation, separating the two illnesses.
Cluster analysis of autonomic function (Fukuda CFS) gave four profiles; sympathetic-dysautonomia phenotype (34%) had more severe disease and lowest quality of life.
Considerations for dental care of homebound ME/CFS patients.
T1w/T2w MRI ratio raised in white matter, subcortical grey matter and brainstem in Fukuda ME/CFS; related to HRV, cognition and respiration rate.
Systematic review of mitochondrial abnormalities found inconsistent results across structure, function, metabolites and coenzymes.
Plasma proteomics associated IGHV3-23/30 with ME/CFS, suggesting antigen-driven B-cell clonal expansion; ML panels AUC 0.77-0.84.
German primary-care CFS diagnoses associated with cancer (OR 2.57), sleep disorders (OR 1.88) and depression (OR 1.77).
Machine learning on N-back fMRI before and after exercise separated CFS from Gulf War illness at about 75-79% accuracy.
note: No healthy control comparison of classifier; modest sample

finding: Opinion on providing compassionate home care for severely affected, housebound ME/CFS patients.
In ME/CFS, titers of beta1/beta2 adrenergic receptor autoantibodies correlated with local structural network measures in right prefrontal and precentral regions.
note: No control group in abstract; weak regional correlations

finding: Preliminary ICF core set: 82-100% had impairments in energy, fatigue, endurance, sleep and pain; half had cognitive and sensory problems.
Preprint of gut fungal dysbiosis in tumour cachexia in mice; ME only as comparator.
Commentary arguing ME/CFS should be treated as biomedical disease, replying to Sharpe and Greco.
N-back working memory worsened after 30-min head-up tilt (2-back correct 77% to 62%, 3-back 57% to 41%) in ME/CFS.
PEM severity associated with onset age 32 or older (OR 1.8), recurrent infections (OR 2.1) and certain precipitants in ICC patients.
Dutch population cohort: new-onset CFS predictors were mostly syndrome-specific, and CFS was more distinct from IBS and FM.
In severe ME/CFS, a 15-min 20-degree tilt reduced cerebral blood flow by 27%, comparable to the 26% decline with 70-degree tilt in milder patients.
Archival data: suicide risk higher in those using the CFS label, with limited function and without comorbid illness.
Childhood trauma did not predict response to group CBT for CDC-defined CFS.
UK ME patient survey: illness duration, trust in GP, diagnosis time and sex predicted GP visits.
SF-36 physical function, steps/day and %peak VO2 were significantly correlated in ME/CFS; single measures inadequate.
Hemin improved behaviour, oxidative stress and neurotransmitters in a mouse forced-swim fatigue model.
Norwegian adolescents with CFS/ME had low quality of life (PedsQL 50), lower in girls; school support associated with better scores.
Response arguing against labelling ME/CFS as 'illness without disease'.
NLP method to extract clinical history segments from CFS assessments.
Actigraphy in PACE: 21% pervasively inactive, 11% pervasively active, 30% boom-and-bust, 38% indeterminate; inactive group more disabled, boom-bust more sleep disturbance.
note: Oxford criteria CFS; baseline before treatment

finding: Adolescents with CFS/ME and comorbid psychopathology endorsed more negative cognitive errors and catastrophising (d 0.5-1.3).
European systematic review: ME/CFS prevalence 0.1-2.2% across scarce studies.
Disequilibrium (eyes-closed postural instability) in 32% and POT in 22% of ME patients; 26% failed the 10-min standing test, 89% of whom had disequilibrium.
Movement-preparation attenuation of laser-evoked potentials was similar in CFS and controls, not supporting impaired motor-induced nociceptive inhibition.
Commentary on potential post-viral depression after COVID-19 and overlap with ME/CFS.
Systematic review of blood and urine metabolomics found inconsistent results across 11 studies.
Partners of CFS patients were less fatigued than controls; female partner fatigue and relationship dissatisfaction predicted CBT outcome.
Systematic review of neuroimaging: differences reported in grey and white matter volume, cerebral blood flow, EEG, connectivity, but heterogeneous.

Resting and exercising muscle membrane excitability (M-wave) altered in 39 patients who also had higher oxidative stress markers and lower exercise K+ outflow; 33 patients had none, indicating subgroups.
note: No healthy control group in abstract; at least four criteria

finding: PBMC miRNA expression after exercise differed by sex and nutritional status in ME/CFS.
PBMC bioenergetics: both moderate and severe ME/CFS had reduced mitochondrial and ATP-linked respiration vs controls; severe had higher respiratory acidification and lower glycolysis once corrected.
PTPN22 rs2476601 (OR 1.63) and CTLA4 rs3087243 (OR 1.53) autoimmunity alleles associated with ME/CFS only in infection-triggered onset.
Nursing overview of CFS pathophysiology, diagnosis and care.
Overview: acupuncture reviews for CFS claimed safety and efficacy but GRADE evidence was low or very low and AMSTAR-2 quality critically low.

n: 170 CFS, 196 CFS/FM, 56 FM, 70 GWI vs 428 controls
finding: Tender-point dolorimetry showed hyperalgesia in CFS (5.8 kg), CFS/FM (3.1) and FM (3.9) versus controls (7.2 kg), p<0.0001.
Psychometric validation of the School and Social Adjustment Scale and SF-36 physical function in adolescent CFS.

n: 161 ME/CFS; controls 15 PBC, 14 FM, 29 MS, 44 donors
finding: Only 1 of 161 ME/CFS patients had anti-PDC antibodies; anti-mitochondrial antibodies negative; metabolic dysfunction not explained by these autoantibodies.
CFS-compatible symptoms in 16% of returning primary antibody deficiency patients (minimum 4% of those surveyed).
Polysomnography in ME/CFS: 70% had increased awakenings, 22% obstructive apnea, 27% periodic limb movements; awakenings correlated with reduced emotional awareness.
Few paediatric CFS/ME treatment studies measured pain, and none targeted it; results mixed.
CDC-defined CFS prevalence 6.76% in Chinese nurses, linked to overcommitment, workplace violence and low support.
Preprint RCT of intranasal mechanical stimulation of vagal nuclei reported about 30% symptom reduction over 8 weeks, with immune correlates around IL-17 axis.
note: Preprint; sample size not in abstract; device trial

finding: HERV-H, -K and -W overexpressed in immune cells of fibromyalgia patients with or without ME/CFS, with raised IFN-beta and IFN-gamma.
Lymphocyte death rate, lymphoblast mitochondrial respiration and TORC1 activity each gave over 90% sensitivity; combined approached 100% sensitivity and specificity.
note: Same group, small sample, no independent validation

finding: In severe ME/CFS (UK ME biobank), routine creatine kinase, plasma EV characteristics and a few PBMC and EV miRNAs were associated with disease.
note: Severe patients; sample size not in abstract

finding: IgG from healthy controls stimulated beta2-adrenergic receptor signalling and modulated monocyte cytokines and T-cell proliferation, but IgG from ME/CFS with high beta2 antibodies did not.
Preprint of Norwegian adolescent CFS/ME quality of life study (PedsQL 50, boys better than girls).
Statistical method for microbiome association testing, applied to colorectal cancer and ME/CFS datasets.
Salivary daily cortisol output (AUCg) was lower in CFS (92.2) than controls (125.5 nmol/l.h), but hair cortisol was not lower.
note: Hair vs saliva dissociation; small; Fukuda-type

finding: Logistic regression on N-back fMRI region activations classified CFS vs sedentary controls at 80% (day 1) and 76% (day 2) accuracy.
Community prevalence of paediatric ME/CFS was 0.75%, higher in African American and Latinx youth; under 5% previously diagnosed.
Australian ME/CFS patients had markedly impaired SF-36 across all domains versus the general population.
Handgrip strength predicted peak VO2 and maximal work rate equally in ME/CFS and non-ME/CFS chronic fatigue.
Linguistic coding of e-consultations agreed with self-reported depression in only 19%.
Eight interventions (e.g. CBT, GET, CoQ10+NADH, rintatolimod) showed significance in individual RCTs but none was definitively effective; 76% used Fukuda criteria.
Reduced HRV with sympathetic predominance in female Fukuda CFS/ME predicted fatigue severity.
Card-ranking study built a conceptual framework of HRQoL in paediatric CFS/ME; symptoms, tiredness and payback/crashing ranked most important.
Summary of methods for documenting ME/CFS disability claims, emphasising PEM and objective impairment.
Occupational therapy review of accommodations for university students with ME/CFS.
After two CPETs 24 h apart, ME/CFS reported 14 symptoms on average vs 4 in controls and still 4 symptoms over the next 7 days (controls none).
Two-day CPET measurements were reliable (moderate to high ICC) and separated ME/CFS from controls with moderate to large effect sizes.
Non-classical CD16A+ monocytes were elevated in patients versus unrelated donors but not versus unaffected family members, arguing the marker is not ME/CFS-specific.
Hours of upright activity were lower in ME/CFS, with greater orthostatic symptoms and interference with daily activities.
NIH funding for ME/CFS about 7% of that commensurate with disease burden; burden about double that of HIV/AIDS.
NK ADCC, CD16A+ NK counts lower in CFS patients and their unaffected relatives than unrelated controls; relatives mostly FCGR3A F/F; low ADCC likely familial risk, not diagnostic.
Lived-experience account of ME affecting treatment of comorbidities.
Thesis on perfectionism and metacognition in comorbid depression and anxiety in CFS/ME.
Lacanian psychoanalytic analysis of interviews with seven people with CFS/ME.
Mouse comparison of LPS, poly I:C and adrenalectomy as CFS models: LPS/poly I:C resembled depression, adrenalectomy gave fatigue-like behaviour and raised TGF-beta1.
Repeated Brucella abortus injections in mice reduced wheel running, raised hippocampal IL-1b, IL-6 and oxidative stress; Kampo medicines lowered cytokines without symptom benefit.
Preprint: NK ADCC and CD16A+ NK counts were lower in both patients and unaffected relatives than unrelated controls, so ADCC is unsuitable as a diagnostic biomarker.
Large cohort showed raised CD4/CD8 ratio and CD8 effector memory, reduced NK in under-50s, and altered Th17, Th1, Th2 and MAIT function; random forest identified 93% of patients.
note: Preprint; same group as Cell Reports Med 2020; n not in abstract

finding: In ME/CFS, plasma beta-NGF related to fatigue; CCL11, CXCL10, IL-7, TNF-a and TGF-b1 related to cognitive impairment and pain, with sex moderating some associations.
41.9% of CFS/ME clinic patients had threshold health anxiety; CBT for health anxiety showed large effects in a case series.
16-week structured exercise programme improved visual attention reaction time in completers; 36% did not complete.
Spanish tertiary patients had worse SF-36 function and more symptoms than US patients.
MAGENTA feasibility phase: recruitment to a trial of GET versus activity management in children was feasible.
Paediatric ME/CFS patients valued early diagnosis, empathetic physicians, self-management and school liaison.

n: 38 ME/CFS, 190 chronic pain vs 29 LPS, 163 primary care, 155 general, 48 healthy
finding: Self-rated sickness behaviour (SicknessQ) in ME/CFS and chronic pain was similar to that of healthy people at peak LPS-induced inflammation.
In Fukuda CFS, high-PEM patients had greater symptom burden and psychological distress than low-PEM patients.
44.7% of ICC ME/CFS patients had resting lactate at or above 2 mmol/L, and these had more severe PEM (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.10-5.55).
Philosophical reply to Sharpe and Greco on 'illness without disease'.
Intimate partner violence exposure associated with higher incidence of fibromyalgia (IRR 1.73) and CFS in women (UK primary care database).
EUROMENE survey: only five countries had national diagnostic guidelines; Fukuda criteria most recommended.
Serum GDF15 higher in severe ME/CFS (602 vs 491 pg/ml in controls, P=0.01) but only marginally in mild/moderate; correlated with fatigue; stable over 7 months.
NK cell TRPM2 and CD38 surface expression higher at baseline in ME/CFS; 8-Br-ADPR altered TRPM2 and NK cytotoxicity.
Three months of recumbent isometric yoga reduced Chalder fatigue (25.3 to 17.0) and changed serum miRNA in nine ME/CFS patients.
Children and parents defined recovery as return to activity, flexibility and absence of payback.
Normalized high-frequency HRV (parasympathetic) was reduced in CFS during deep sleep but not wakefulness; slower sleep onset, more awakenings, more slow-wave sleep.
Urinary 1H-NMR after a detoxification challenge separated high from low fatigue groups; no clear biomarker emerged.
note: Fatigue scale based, not ME/CFS criteria

finding: Simulation model hypothesising Treg-controlled chronic herpesvirus responses explain raised Tregs in ME/CFS.
Achilles tendon stiffness related to quality of life in fatigued Gaucher disease patients.
Circulating EVs were increased in ME/CFS (AUC 0.80) and EV proteins talin-1, filamin-A and 14-3-3 were the most abundant discriminating proteins versus controls, idiopathic fatigue and depression.
note: Sample size not in abstract; two independent proteomic analyses

finding: Cognitive interviews pretested a paediatric CFS/ME patient-reported outcome measure.
UK ME/CFS Biobank risk-factor analysis: frequent colds (OR 8.26) and recent infection before onset distinguished ME/CFS, especially from MS.
68% had current or lifetime psychiatric diagnosis, which raised mental fatigue but did not multiply physical symptoms; 81% had FM, IBS or MCS.
DSQ-2 and SF-36 with machine learning separated ME/CFS from post-polio syndrome mainly on neurocognitive, PEM and neuroendocrine domains.
Two months of seated isometric yoga reduced Chalder fatigue (P=0.002) and depression, with no change in cortisol, cytokines, BDNF or HRV.
Patch-clamp confirmed impaired TRPM3 function in IL-2 stimulated NK cells from ME/CFS; naltrexone restored function in vitro.
Review proposing metformin, Momordica charantia, meldonium, dichloroacetate and nutraceuticals plus comorbidity management.
fMRI showed brainstem reticular connectivity deficits (medulla to cuneiform nucleus, to hippocampus and thalamus) in Fukuda ME/CFS, only during task, related to symptom severity.
Implementation of stepped internet CBT then face-to-face CBT in Dutch routine care; outcomes compared to RCT benchmark.
CFS/ME and fibromyalgia showed similar symptom patterns on questionnaires.
In a UK CFS service, 29% had stopped work; older age, poor functioning and depression were associated with permanently interrupted employment.
Preprint of the natural-history framework: early hypermetabolic neuro-immune stage progressing to hypometabolic state.
Narrative of one woman's recovery from CFS analysed through posthuman theory.
PROMIS Fatigue Short Form 7a showed good reliability and known-groups validity in ME/CFS (mean T-score 68.6).
note: Outcome measure validation; Multi-Site Clinical Assessment

finding: Five miRNAs (miR-558, -146a, -150, -124, -143) were downregulated in adolescent CFS and correlated with pain and IL-6, TNF-a, COX-2.
note: Adolescents; patients had higher pain thresholds than controls

finding: DSQ-2 validation with eight symptom factors including PEM and orthostatic intolerance.
Commercial mitochondrial energy score showed no difference between CFS/ME and controls and was highly sensitive to 24-hour sample processing delay.
note: Small; important caution for commercial tests

finding: Scoping review of paediatric CFS/ME management: graded exercise, CBT and multifaceted programmes reported to reduce fatigue; few nutrition studies.
Gulf War illness serum metabolomics showed lipid abnormalities; most pathways shared with male ME/CFS were regulated in the opposite direction.
note: GWI cohort; comparison to published ME/CFS data

finding: Serum activin B differed between ME/CFS (CCC/ICC) and controls but median was lower in ME/CFS in this cohort, opposite to a pilot; random forest on routine pathology gave at least 62% prediction.
14-item short form of the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire differentiates ME/CFS from controls.
Relationship dissatisfaction related to fatigue via depression and communication satisfaction.
Machine-learning multiclass classifiers on gut microbiome distinguished six diseases including ME/CFS best at genus level.
Review of inflammatory, neuroinflammatory and metabolic abnormalities as basis for ME/CFS biomarkers.
Serum/urine metabolomics: hypoxanthine fell with PEM severity, glucose:lactate ratio shifted, and urinary methylhistidine, mannitol and acetate rose, suggesting hypermetabolism and hypoacetylation.
Guidance on documenting disability in ME/CFS cases, noting frequent orthostatic intolerance in children.
Spanish ME/CFS cohort: 58.6% unemployed; autonomic dysfunction (OR 2.21), fatigue, pain and sleep dysfunction associated with work disability.
Freedom of Information survey found English ME/CFS clinics inconsistently monitored treatment harms and reported none despite dropouts.
Symptom-overlap survey: pain increasing the day after activity in 85% of CFS and 94% of FM; generic functional symptom scale developed.
Essay arguing for illness-focused psychological and behavioural treatments for CFS.
Acupuncture improved response rate vs sham (RR 2.08, 95% CI 1.4-3.1, low certainty); most trials low quality.
Hypothesis that impaired PDC E3 subunit lowers dihydrolipoic acid regeneration, causing hyperlactataemia and PEM.
hsCRP higher in CFS and FM than controls after adjustment for BMI (p<0.001), with no difference between patient groups.
note: Women only; CRP strongly BMI dependent

finding: Objective neuropsychological deficits in CFS were mainly in psychomotor speed and attention and were weakly related to subjective cognitive complaints.
Dizziness while recumbent in 41% and standing in 72% of CFS; POTS in 6 and exercise-induced START tachycardia in 10; tachycardia did not explain OI symptoms.
Title reports reduced glycolytic reserve in isolated NK cells from ME/CFS patients (preliminary).
note: Abstract supplied is for an unrelated juvenile arthritis IL-6 study (record mismatch); finding taken from title only; n unknown

finding: ASL cerebral blood flow and HRV did not differ between CFS and controls, but higher CBF and HRV power were associated with lower fatigue within CFS.
23andMe exome-region SNP comparison with Kaviar found 5693 SNPs at least twofold different, enriched in immune, hormone and metabolic pathways.
note: Pilot with public reference controls, ancestry and platform biases; no formal association testing

finding: CBRQ and its short form showed good reliability and validity in adolescent CFS.
